q: 1. The final setting time of ordinary Portland cement should not be less than .....
explain: As per the answer key, option c (10 h). Note: the usual code limit is that final setting time should not be MORE than 10 hours, so this question is worded oddly in the book.

q: 2. The initial and final setting times of quick setting cement are .....
explain: Quick setting cement has an initial setting time of about 5 minutes and a final setting time of about 30 minutes.

q: 3. Excessive free lime and excessive magnesia present in the cement make the cement .....
options: to have very low initial setting time
to have very low compressive strength
explain: Free lime and magnesia hydrate slowly after setting and expand, causing cracks and disintegration; such cement is unsound.

q: 4. In the cement the compound quickest to react with water, is
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts almost instantly with water, causing flash set if not controlled by gypsum.

q: 5. Rapid hardening cement contains
explain: Rapid hardening cement has a higher C3S content, which speeds up early strength development.

q: 6. The percentage of the residue left after sieving good Portland cement in 90 micron sieve should not exceed .....
explain: For fineness, the residue on a 90 micron IS sieve should not exceed 10%.

q: 7. White cement should have least percentage of
explain: Iron oxide imparts grey/brown color to ordinary cement, so white cement is made with minimal iron oxide.

q: 8. The sand is mixed with lime mortar to .....
explain: Sand is an inert filler that reduces shrinkage and cracking of lime mortar and makes it porous so CO2 can reach it.

q: 9. The insoluble residue in cement is less than
explain: Specifications limit the insoluble residue (impurities) in cement to less than about 1.5%.

q: 10. Quick lime is
explain: Quicklime is chemically calcium oxide (CaO), produced by burning (calcining) limestone.

q: 11. The aggregate is called coarse aggregate if it is completely retained on .....
explain: Aggregate retained on the 4.75 mm IS sieve is coarse aggregate. (The book prints option d with an 's)' label.)

q: 12. The volume of one bag of cement weighing 50 kg is
explain: A standard 50 kg bag of cement occupies a volume of about 0.0345 cubic meters, based on cement's bulk density.

q: 13. To retard the initial setting time of cement, the compound responsible, is .....
explain: Gypsum is added (about 2 to 3%) to control the quick setting caused by C3A.

q: 14. Oilwell cement is generally used for .....
explain: Oil well cement is specially made to set properly at the high temperature and pressure found in oil wells.

q: 15. The main constituents which imparts hydraulicity to hydraulic lime is .....
explain: As per the answer key, clay (silica, alumina and iron oxide in clay) gives lime its hydraulicity.

q: 16. The lime which contains high percentage of calcium oxide, is generally called .....
explain: As per the answer key, fat lime, which is high in calcium oxide and slakes vigorously with a large increase in volume. 'Rich lime' also describes it, but the key gives a.

q: 17. Stetting time of hydraulic lime is
explain: The setting time for hydraulic lime varies significantly based on its classification (feebly, moderately, or eminently hydraulic), often spanning from hours to weeks.

q: 18. Lime having high calcium oxide content, which can set and become hard only in the presence of CO2 from the atmosphere is known as
explain: Fat lime (or rich lime) consists of high CaO content and hardens through carbonation, a process requiring CO2 from the air.

q: 19. Sand is mixed with lime mortar to
options: helps the pure lime to set by allowing penetration of air
explain: Sand acts as an inert filler that improves workability, prevents shrinkage cracks, reduces costs, and allows CO2 to penetrate for setting.

q: 20. The lime mortar in which ash or cinder is used as fine aggregate is called
explain: When ash or cinder replaces sand as fine aggregate in lime mortar, it is termed black mortar due to its dark color.

q: 21. A dry powder obtained on treating quick lime with just enough water... is called
explain: When just enough water is added to quicklime to complete the chemical reaction without making it a paste, it results in a dry powder called hydrated lime.

q: 22. Plaster of paris can be obtained from the calcinations of
explain: Heating gypsum ($CaSO_4 cdot 2H_2O$) to approximately $150^{circ}C$ removes most of its water, creating Plaster of Paris ($CaSO_4 cdot 0.5H_2O$).

q: 23. Gypsum is added to cement for reducing the fast reacting property of
explain: Tricalcium aluminate ($C_3A$) reacts very quickly with water. Gypsum is added to control this reaction and prevent 'flash set'.

q: 24. The constituents of cement, which act as binder are
options: dicalcium silicate, tricalcium silicate and carbon
tricalcium aluminate, tricalcium silicate and carbon
explain: While the option mentions carbon (likely an error in the source text), Silicates (C2S and C3S) are the primary binding agents responsible for strength.

q: 25. When water is added to cement... an increase in temperature occurs... is called
explain: Hydration is an exothermic chemical reaction; the heat released during this process is specifically called the 'heat of hydration'.

q: 26. Dormant period (2-5hr) is concerned with
explain: The dormant period is a stage in the hydration process where the reaction rate slows down significantly, allowing for the placement and finishing of concrete.

q: 27. The amount of loss of ignition, insoluble residue & residual retained (OPC) on IS sieve
explain: Standard limits for OPC: Loss on Ignition (<4%), Insoluble Residue (<1.5%), and Sieve Residue (<10%).

q: 28. The strength of RHPC for one day is equal to... day of PPC
explain: Rapid Hardening Portland Cement (RHPC) is designed to achieve the 3-day strength of ordinary cement in just 1 day.

q: 29. The possibility of bleeding, segregation and laitance is reduced by
explain: Air entraining agents create tiny bubbles that improve workability and cohesion, thereby reducing bleeding and segregation.

q: 30. Workability is tested by
explain: Workability is measured using several methods including Slump, Compacting Factor (C.F.), and Vee-Bee consistometer tests.

q: 31. The most commonly used accelerator for concreting is
explain: Calcium chloride is the most widely used and cheapest accelerator for increasing the rate of hydration.

q: 32. The minimum percentage of silica, alumina and ferric oxide in lime for white washing, is .....
explain: Fat lime for white-washing is pure, so it needs no clayey impurities; the minimum is 0.

q: 33. The initial setting time of lime-pozzolana, is .....
explain: As per the answer key, the initial setting time of lime-pozzolana is 120 minutes.

q: 34. Excessive free lime and excessive magnesia present in the cement make the cement
options: to have very low initial setting time
to have very light compressive strength
explain: Free lime and magnesia hydrate very slowly, causing expansion and cracking after the cement has set, making it 'unsound'.

q: 35. Portland cement manufactured from pure white chalk and clay but free from iron oxide, is known as
explain: Iron oxide provides the grey color to cement; by removing it, white cement is produced for architectural use.

q: 36. Le Chatelier's device is used for determining the
explain: Le Chatelier's apparatus measures the expansion of cement paste, which indicates its soundness.

q: 37. The initial setting time for ordinary Portland cement should not be less than
explain: As per IS specification, OPC must have an initial setting time of not less than 30 minutes to allow adequate working time.

q: 38. The quality of cement is good if it has more of
explain: High C3S content ensures better early strength and binding quality in Portland cement.

q: 39. Quick setting cement is used
options: where resistance to acidic water is required
explain: Quick-setting cement is essential for underwater work where the cement must set before being washed away by currents.

q: 40. Snowcem is
explain: Snowcem is a well-known brand of waterproof cement paint used on exterior masonry surfaces.

q: 41. Compared to the ordinary portland cement, the ultimate strength of the pozzolona portland cement is
explain: While slow to start, PPC eventually achieves a higher ultimate strength due to the formation of additional calcium silicate hydrates.

q: 42. In the chemical composition of test for loss on ignition, the cement is treated to a temperature of
explain: Loss on ignition involves heating a sample to 900-1000°C until constant weight is reached.

q: 43. Loss on ignition in cement should not exceed
explain: Standard specifications limit Loss on Ignition to a maximum of 4% for OPC.

q: 44. The insoluble residues in good cement should be
explain: Insoluble residue indicates the purity of the cement and should be less than 1.5%.

q: 45. During the test of portland cement for “loss of ignition” the loss in weight occurs due to
explain: High temperature drives off moisture and CO2 from carbonates present in the sample.

q: 46. Storage of cement should be done on
explain: Cement must be kept on a raised, dry platform away from walls to prevent moisture absorption.

q: 47. The cement mortar mix generally used for internal plaster
explain: For internal plastering, a 1:4 mix (one part cement to four parts sand) is standard as it provides a good balance of workability and strength without excessive shrinkage.

q: 48. The proportions of lime and sand in the mortar normally used in brick construction are
explain: A lime to sand ratio of about 1:6 is commonly used in ordinary brick masonry mortar.

q: 49. The main constituent of a Portland cement is:
explain: Lime is the principal constituent by weight in Portland cement, forming the basis of its cementing compounds.

q: 50. Humidity causes...........of cement in bag.
explain: Moisture in the air reacts with cement (hydration), causing it to set or form hard lumps inside the bag, which reduces its quality.

q: 51. Reduction in aggregate cement ratio while keeping W/C ratio constant causes
explain: If the cement content increases (ratio decreases) while water remains proportional, there is more paste to lubricate the aggregates, increasing workability.

q: 52. Thermal characteristics is observed when
options: water is added to slaked lime
water is added to fat lime
explain: The key specifies 'a' (stones), though usually, this refers to the exothermic reaction of adding water to lime (slaking).
